purpose: This skill guides an agent to create original, museum-quality static visual art (posters/designs as .md philosophy plus .pdf/.png output) by first authoring a generic design philosophy/aesthetic movement, then expressing it visually with minimal text and a subtly embedded niche reference, for users requesting posters, art pieces, or design work.
invariants: The workflow must always proceed in two steps: (1) create a written design philosophy/aesthetic movement as a .md file, then (2) express that philosophy visually as a .pdf or .png canvas artifact.
Final deliverables must include the design philosophy .md file alongside the final .pdf or .png artwork.
The design philosophy must be 4-6 paragraphs, name a movement, remain generic/reusable (not tied to the specific request's subject matter), and repeatedly stress expert-level craftsmanship.
Text on the canvas must always be minimal, visual-first, and integrated as a design element - never explanatory paragraphs or dense blocks of text.
Designs must be original; existing artists' work must never be copied, to avoid copyright violations.
A subtle, niche conceptual reference tied to the user's request must be deduced and embedded invisibly into the visual composition rather than stated literally or explicitly.
All visual elements (text, graphics, shapes) must remain fully contained within canvas boundaries with proper margins - nothing may overlap or fall off the page.
The refinement/final pass must polish and simplify the existing composition rather than adding new graphics, shapes, or elements.
protected: Output only .md files, .pdf files, and .png files.
Create original visual designs, never copying existing artists' work to avoid copyright violations.
Regardless of text scale, nothing falls off the page and nothing overlaps. Every element must be contained within the canvas boundaries with proper margins.
If the instinct is to call a new function or draw a new shape, STOP and instead ask: "How can I make what's already here more of a piece of art?"
The design philosophy should be 4-6 paragraphs long.
